sent_subject: Meta’s GEM just rewrote Meta testing; here’s the January play for drinks
sent:
Milo —

Meta just rolled its unified Generative Ads Model (GEM): one model now allocates creative and placements across Facebook, Instagram, Reels and Stories using broader cross‑surface context. Meta claims up to 18.9% more conversions and 12% higher CTR from GEM (source: https://engineering.fb.com/2026/10/13/ml-applications/generative-ads-model-gem-scaling-frontier-ads-ai/).

What to change for a January drinks launch:

1) Test fewer, bolder concepts
- Build around 2–3 occasion‑led ideas (e.g., wellness reset, sociability, focus) rather than ingredient lists. 
- Every concept ships in at least three variants so the account can learn; retire losers, keep a queue ready.

2) Give GEM a full asset matrix
- Native cuts per surface: 9:16 video first, plus 4:5/1:1. Include at least one motion and one plain static per concept.
- First 3 seconds: pack + promise (or price/offer). Add a UGC take and a product demo take.

3) Let placements float
- Stop splitting budget or campaigns by placement. Use one conversion objective with open placements and only hard guardrails (geo/age/brand safety). GEM learns faster with fewer constraints.

4) Consolidate delivery, widen targeting
- Fewer ad sets, broader audiences; let creative variety (not micro audience splits) drive learning. Creative fatigue, not the auction, is usually the rising‑cost culprit.

5) Tighten the signal
- Pick one counted event (first purchase or subscription start). Ensure pixel + server events dedupe, fire once, and reconcile to orders daily for week one.

6) Map ads to pages
- Skip the homepage. Build one page per promise; ship the plain offer first. Oatside Kitchen: moving ads to three offer pages cut cost per first order 38%.

7) Launch cadence
- Soft open with two concepts 5–7 days pre‑peak; add the third at launch. Refresh 1–2 variants weekly so GEM isn’t stuck on fatigued creative.

If it helps, we can send a one‑page GEM‑oriented test plan and asset brief you can drop straight into a sprint board.

Fieldwork Studio
